options: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory
quiz.explanation: The University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory anchor Chicago's quantum technology hub, the Chicago Quantum Exchange.

laws.title: Ranked Choice Voting Pilot Programs
laws.subtitle: Illinois Cities Test Alternative Voting Methods
laws.fullDescription: Several Illinois municipalities piloted ranked choice voting for local elections, allowing voters to rank candidates by preference. Proponents argued RCV produced more representative outcomes and reduced negative campaigning. Chicago considered adoption for its mayoral race. Illinois joined a growing movement of jurisdictions experimenting with electoral reform.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; election administration compliance
exceptions: State law primacy over municipal methods
Accessibility requirements for ballot design

quiz.q: What does ranked choice voting allow voters to do?
quiz.explanation: Ranked choice voting allows voters to rank candidates in order of preference, with last-place candidates eliminated and their votes redistributed until a winner emerges.

laws.title: Coal Plant Closures and Clean Energy Transition
laws.subtitle: Illinois Accelerates Coal Phase-Out
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Clean Energy Jobs Act mandated a coal phase-out timeline with the last coal plants closing by 2045 and 100% clean electricity by 2050. Commonwealth Edison and Ameren Illinois replaced coal with wind, solar, and battery storage. Nuclear plants were given state support to continue operations as clean baseload.
laws.penalty: Carbon standards fines for early coal plant operations
exceptions: Just transition funds for coal communities
Reliability emergency provisions

quiz.q: By when does Illinois's law require 100% clean electricity?
quiz.explanation: Illinois's Clean Energy Jobs Act mandates 100% clean electricity by 2050, with coal plants phased out by 2045.

laws.title: Chicago Tech Hub and Midwest Innovation Economy
laws.subtitle: Chicago emerges as national tech hub beyond coastal concentrations
laws.fullDescription: Chicago has emerged as a major technology and innovation hub, ranked third in the US for tech job growth. The city's strengths include financial technology (trading infrastructure), supply chain technology, and enterprise software. Major tech companies have expanded Chicago offices. The Illinois Quantum Economic Development Consortium and quantum computing research attract deep tech investment. Chicago's advantages include lower costs than coastal cities, strong universities, and central location for national operations.
laws.penalty: Technology companies receiving Illinois incentives must meet job creation and retention requirements
exceptions: Startup companies under headcount thresholds qualify for lighter reporting requirements
University spinouts receive special innovation zone tax treatment

laws.title: Agricultural Biotech Hub and Gene Editing Regulations
laws.subtitle: Illinois hosts world's agricultural biotechnology giants
laws.fullDescription: Illinois is home to Corteva, GATX, and the headquarters of agricultural biotech giants Syngenta, Dekalb/Bayer Crop Science, and others. The state's agricultural research institutions and proximity to major farming regions make it a global biotech hub. Gene editing technology (CRISPR) is reshaping crop development, with US regulations treating gene-edited crops differently from GMOs. Illinois farmers adopt biotech crops at high rates. The regulatory distinction between gene editing and traditional GMOs shapes global trade.
laws.penalty: Biotech crop approvals require EPA, USDA, and FDA review before commercial release
exceptions: CRISPR-edited crops that could occur naturally don't require USDA regulatory review
Research field trials have separate approval pathway from commercial release

laws.title: Pension Crisis and Fiscal Sustainability
laws.subtitle: Illinois's pension debt threatens long-term fiscal viability
laws.fullDescription: Illinois has the worst-funded pension system of any US state, with over $200 billion in unfunded pension liabilities — a constitutional obligation from decades of underfunding. The Illinois constitution prohibits diminishing public pension benefits, making reform legally constrained. Illinois loses population annually partly due to high taxes needed to service debt. The state is caught in a fiscal doom loop: pension payments crowd out other spending, forcing tax increases, which drive residents out, reducing the tax base.
laws.penalty: Pension benefits are constitutionally protected and cannot be reduced; underfunding triggers mandatory catch-up contributions
exceptions: New government employees hired after pension reform dates participate in different benefit tiers
Municipalities can seek state restructuring assistance for extreme fiscal distress

quiz.q: What makes Illinois's pension crisis particularly hard to solve?
options: Federal law prevents state pension reform
The Illinois constitution prohibits diminishing public pension benefits
Pension funds are invested in risky assets
Illinois lacks tax authority to raise revenue
quiz.explanation: The Illinois constitution explicitly protects public pension benefits from reduction — meaning unlike other states, Illinois cannot legally reduce promised benefits even as unfunded liabilities exceed $200 billion.

laws.title: Chicago Pension Crisis and Municipal Fiscal Stress
laws.subtitle: Illinois and Chicago struggling with massive unfunded pension obligations
laws.fullDescription: Illinois and the city of Chicago carry some of the nation's largest unfunded public pension obligations — Chicago alone faces pension debts estimated at over $30 billion across its various pension funds. The state of Illinois has approximately $200 billion in unfunded pension liabilities, the worst in the nation relative to state revenues. Illinois's constitution protects pension benefits from reduction, limiting the state's options for reform. The pension crisis has resulted in years of below-investment-grade credit ratings for Chicago, higher borrowing costs, and difficult tradeoffs between pension contributions and other city services. Population decline — Chicago has lost hundreds of thousands of residents over the past two decades — reduces the tax base while fixed pension obligations remain. The state has the highest property taxes in the nation partly due to local government fiscal stress. Pension crisis dynamics serve as a warning to other cities and states with underfunded retirement obligations.
laws.penalty: Government entities that fail to make required pension contributions face legal obligations; bond payment defaults trigger legal proceedings
exceptions: Illinois constitution's pension protection clause limits what reforms are legally possible without constitutional amendment

quiz.q: What constitutional provision makes Illinois pension reform particularly difficult?
options: A balanced budget amendment preventing new spending
Illinois's constitution protects pension benefits from reduction
A supermajority requirement for any pension changes
Federal ERISA law preventing state modifications to public pensions
quiz.explanation: Illinois's state constitution explicitly protects public pension benefits from reduction, severely limiting the state's legal options for pension reform even as unfunded liabilities approach $200 billion.

laws.title: BIPA Biometric Privacy and Facial Recognition Liability
laws.subtitle: Illinois leading nation on biometric data protection
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA), passed in 2008, is one of the most important and impactful privacy laws in the United States. BIPA requires informed written consent before collecting biometric data (fingerprints, face geometry, retina scans, voiceprints), mandates a retention schedule, prohibits profit from biometric data, and — most significantly — creates a private right of action with statutory damages of $1,000-5,000 per violation. This enforcement mechanism has generated some of the largest privacy class action settlements in US history, including a $650 million settlement from Facebook and $228 million from Google's YouTube. Companies across industries including retail, healthcare, hospitality, and technology have faced BIPA suits for using facial recognition without consent. Illinois has inspired similar legislation in other states and federal proposals.
laws.penalty: BIPA violations carry statutory damages of $1,000 per negligent violation or $5,000 per intentional or reckless violation; class action exposure has generated billion-dollar settlements
exceptions: Financial institutions subject to Gramm-Leach-Bliley, government agencies, and certain employment applications may have different requirements

quiz.q: What makes Illinois's BIPA particularly powerful compared to most other privacy laws?
options: It completely bans all biometric data collection
It creates a private right of action allowing individuals to sue with statutory damages
It requires government approval for all facial recognition use
It mandates encryption standards for all biometric storage
quiz.explanation: BIPA's private right of action with statutory damages of $1,000-5,000 per violation makes it particularly powerful — class actions against major tech companies have generated settlements in the hundreds of millions to billions of dollars.

laws.title: Climate Action Plan and Coal Plant Phase-Out
laws.subtitle: Illinois transitioning from coal while protecting workers
laws.fullDescription: Illinois passed the Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) in 2021, committing to 100% clean energy by 2045, closing coal power plants on a defined schedule, and creating a $40+ million program supporting workers and communities in coal-dependent areas. Illinois has been heavily dependent on coal power, though coal's share has declined. The state also has significant nuclear power capacity (operated by Exelon/Constellation), which is being retained and supported as zero-carbon generation. Illinois has set ambitious electric vehicle adoption targets and is developing EV charging infrastructure. The climate law attempts to balance environmental goals with economic justice — ensuring that communities most affected by pollution benefit from the clean energy transition and that workers in fossil fuel industries receive transition support.
laws.penalty: Renewable energy portfolio standard requirements carry compliance fees for utilities that fail to meet targets
exceptions: Nuclear power plants receive zero emission credits supporting their continued operation under CEJA
laws.sourceLabel: Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act

quiz.q: What clean energy target did Illinois's Climate and Equitable Jobs Act set?
quiz.explanation: Illinois's Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) committed the state to 100% clean energy by 2045, with a defined schedule for closing coal power plants and significant support programs for affected workers and communities.

laws.title: Democratic Primary Gerrymander Wars
laws.subtitle: Illinois redraws maps to protect Democratic supermajority
laws.fullDescription: Illinois Democrats used their supermajority in the legislature to draw highly gerrymandered congressional and legislative maps, creating safe Democratic districts that critics called the most extreme partisan gerrymander in state history. The maps produced predictable results with Democrats winning lopsided majorities in elections. Illinois serves as a counterexample used by Democrats when criticized for fighting Republican gerrymandering in other states. The Supreme Court's Rucho decision left partisan gerrymandering as a political question beyond federal court review.
laws.penalty: Maps challenged under state constitution's redistricting provisions; Illinois Supreme Court reviews challenges
exceptions: Federal courts cannot hear partisan gerrymandering claims after Rucho
State courts retain jurisdiction under state constitutional claims

quiz.q: What Supreme Court decision left partisan gerrymandering beyond the reach of federal courts?
quiz.explanation: The Supreme Court's 2019 Rucho v. Common Cause decision held that federal courts cannot hear partisan gerrymandering claims, leaving the practice as a political question—allowing both parties to continue drawing maps for partisan advantage.

laws.title: BIPA Biometric Privacy Pioneer
laws.subtitle: Illinois law becomes gold standard for biometric data protection
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA), passed in 2008, has become the nation's most significant biometric privacy law. It requires companies to obtain written consent before collecting biometric data like fingerprints, face scans and iris patterns. BIPA allows private lawsuits with statutory damages, leading to billions in settlements against companies including Facebook, TikTok, Amazon and many smaller firms. BIPA has influenced biometric privacy laws in other states and federal proposals.
laws.penalty: Violations of BIPA carry $1,000 per negligent violation and $5,000 per intentional violation; class actions permitted
exceptions: Employee fingerprint scanning for timekeeping requires consent with specific procedures
Government entities largely exempt from BIPA requirements

quiz.q: What is the maximum statutory damage for intentional BIPA violations?
quiz.explanation: Illinois BIPA carries statutory damages of $5,000 per intentional violation, which combined with class action lawsuits has led to multi-billion dollar settlements against companies that collected biometric data without proper consent.

laws.title: Pension Crisis and Fiscal Stress
laws.subtitle: Illinois carries nation's largest unfunded pension liability
laws.fullDescription: Illinois has the nation's most severe state pension crisis, with over $200 billion in unfunded pension liabilities. The Illinois Supreme Court has ruled that pension benefits constitutionally cannot be reduced, locking in obligations. The state's credit rating has been the lowest of any state. Chicago faces particularly acute pension stress for police, fire and teacher pensions. Despite pension reform attempts, the constitutional protection makes restructuring legally impossible without amendment. The fiscal burden crowds out spending on education, infrastructure and services.
laws.penalty: Pension obligations constitutionally protected; failure to make required payments triggers credit downgrade and borrowing cost increases
exceptions: Future employees can be offered different benefit tiers
Voluntary buyout programs for existing workers have been offered

quiz.q: Approximately how much in unfunded pension liabilities does Illinois carry?
quiz.explanation: Illinois carries over $200 billion in unfunded pension liabilities—the nation's largest—and the Illinois Supreme Court has ruled these obligations constitutionally protected from reduction, making the fiscal burden extremely difficult to address.

laws.title: Climate and Equitable Jobs Act
laws.subtitle: Illinois Coal Phase-Out and Clean Energy Jobs
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's 2021 CEJA law sets a path to 100% clean energy by 2050, phases out all coal plants by 2030, and creates 40,000+ clean energy jobs. A groundbreaking feature is the Clean Jobs Workforce Network, prioritizing hiring from communities that lost fossil fuel jobs and environmental justice communities. The law also provides utility bill assistance to low-income households and prevents the closure of nuclear plants that provide about half of Illinois's carbon-free electricity.
laws.penalty: Utilities failing to meet renewable portfolio standards face alternative compliance payments
exceptions: Nuclear plants receive zero-emission credits to stay operational
Peaker plants retained for grid reliability

laws.title: Illinois Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act
laws.subtitle: No Out-of-Pocket Costs for Rape Kits
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act (SASETA) ensures that sexual assault survivors receive forensic examinations (rape kits) at no cost, with all costs covered by the state's Crime Victims Compensation Program. Illinois also requires hospitals to notify law enforcement within 72 hours (with survivor consent) and provide information about emergency contraception and prophylactic antibiotics. The law mandates 24/7 access to sexual assault nurse examiners at participating hospitals and a trauma-informed approach to survivor care.
laws.penalty: Hospitals not complying face state program funding consequences
exceptions: Survivors can decline forensic examination
Law enforcement notification only with survivor consent

laws.title: Illinois Worker Rights Amendment
laws.subtitle: Constitutional Right to Organize
laws.fullDescription: In November 2022, Illinois voters approved the Illinois Worker Rights Amendment to the state constitution, making Illinois the first state to enshrine the right to organize and bargain collectively in its constitution. The amendment prohibits laws that impair workers' right to organize or that exclude workers from collective bargaining. The amendment effectively bans right-to-work laws in Illinois. Illinois also has a $15 minimum wage (phased in through 2025) and strong prevailing wage laws for public construction. Chicago passed the country's first gig worker minimum pay protection law.
laws.penalty: Constitutional violations actionable in court; unfair labor practices: NLRB and state enforcement; prevailing wage violations: debarment
exceptions: Public safety employees under different collective bargaining framework
Very small employers under different thresholds

laws.title: Illinois Free College for Low-Income Students
laws.subtitle: AIM High Grant
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's AIM HIGH grant program provides free tuition at public universities for students from families earning under $67,100/year (2024). Illinois's public school system is notably unequal — property tax-based school funding creates extreme disparities between wealthy suburban and poor urban/rural districts. Chicago Public Schools (CPS) is the nation's third-largest district. Illinois passed a landmark school funding reform in 2017, moving toward evidence-based funding that accounts for district poverty. Chicago teachers have conducted multiple strikes (2012, 2019) that drew national attention to funding equity and working conditions.
laws.penalty: AIM HIGH grant recipients must maintain academic standards; school funding formula compliance enforced by ISBE
exceptions: Private universities ineligible for the direct grant
Students must be Illinois residents

laws.title: Illinois TRUST Act
laws.subtitle: Illinois's restrictions on immigration detainers
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's TRUST Act (2017) prohibits state and local law enforcement from detaining a person solely based on an ICE detainer request (a request to hold someone beyond their release date for immigration purposes). Illinois also provides drivers' licenses to undocumented residents (since 2013), extended in-state tuition to undocumented students (2003), and enacted the New Americans Executive Order. Illinois has approximately 450,000 undocumented immigrants. Chicago has long been a sanctuary city. These policies have been contrasted with neighboring Indiana's stricter approach.
laws.penalty: Law enforcement officials detaining individuals solely on ICE civil detainers may expose local governments to civil rights liability; state funding conditioned on compliance with TRUST Act

Federal immigration enforcement can still operate in Illinois independently

laws.title: Cannabis Regulation and Tax Act
laws.subtitle: Illinois's cannabis legalization with automatic expungement
laws.fullDescription: Illinois legalized recreational cannabis in 2020 (effective January 1, 2020), becoming the first state to do so through the legislature rather than ballot initiative. Illinois's law included automatic expungement of prior cannabis convictions (over 500,000 records cleared), social equity provisions, and a 25-35% excise tax structure. Illinois maintains criminal penalties for possession above legal limits and all hard drug possession.

Home cultivation prohibited for recreational users in Illinois

laws.title: Illinois Human Rights Act LGBTQ+ Protections
laws.subtitle: Illinois's comprehensive LGBTQ+ legal framework
laws.fullDescription: Illinois has comprehensive LGBTQ+ protections through its Human Rights Act. Illinois prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, education, and public accommodations. Illinois legalized same-sex civil unions (2011) and same-sex marriage (2013, before the Supreme Court). Illinois bans conversion therapy for minors. Illinois was the first state to decriminalize homosexuality (1962). The Illinois LGBTQ+ Senior Task Force works on elder care issues. Illinois also provides gender marker changes on state IDs and birth certificates.

Small housing providers (owner-occupied, less than 2 units) have limited exemptions

quiz.explanation: Illinois became the first US state to decriminalize consensual same-sex activity in 1961 (effective 1962), removing it from its criminal code — predating the Supreme Court's Lawrence v. Texas ruling by 40 years.

laws.title: Strong Shield Law and Robust Press Freedom
laws.subtitle: Illinois has one of the strongest reporter privilege laws in the nation
laws.fullDescription: Illinois enacted one of the first and strongest reporter shield laws in the US (735 ILCS 5/8-901 through 8-909), providing qualified privilege against compelled disclosure of sources and notes. The Illinois shield law protects both confidential and non-confidential sources in civil proceedings. Illinois also has the Freedom of Information Act for government transparency. Chicago is a major journalism hub, home to the Chicago Tribune and many investigative outlets. Illinois journalists have a long tradition of muckraking journalism. quiz.q: What type of sources does Illinois's shield law protect, distinguishing it from some other states?
quiz.explanation: Illinois's shield law is notable for protecting both confidential and non-confidential sources in civil proceedings — a broader protection than many other states that only shield confidential sources.

laws.title: BIPA — Biometric Data Privacy Pioneer
laws.subtitle: Illinois's Biometric Information Privacy Act is the nation's strongest biometric data law
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA, 2008) was the first and remains the strongest US law protecting biometric data — including facial recognition used in social media photo-tagging. BIPA requires informed written consent before collecting biometric identifiers, prohibits sale of biometric data, and provides a private right of action. Facebook paid $650 million to settle a BIPA class action over its facial recognition tag suggestion. TikTok paid $92 million. BIPA has driven major settlements and changed how social media platforms handle facial recognition globally.
laws.penalty: $1,000 per negligent violation and $5,000 per intentional violation; private right of action has generated massive class action settlements
exceptions: Financial institutions subject to GLBA are exempt; some narrow exceptions

quiz.q: What did Facebook pay to settle an Illinois BIPA class action over facial recognition?
quiz.explanation: Facebook paid $650 million to settle a class action lawsuit under Illinois's BIPA over its facial recognition photo-tagging feature — one of the largest privacy settlements in US history, demonstrating BIPA's powerful enforcement through private rights of action.

laws.title: Illinois Transmitters of Money Act and Community Banking
laws.subtitle: Illinois regulates money transmission and has a strong community banking tradition
laws.fullDescription: Illinois regulates money transmission through the Transmitters of Money Act, requiring licenses for businesses that send or receive money including digital assets. Illinois's Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR) oversees banking. Chicago is a major financial center home to major futures exchanges (CME Group, CBOE) and commodities trading. Illinois has strong community banking and credit union presence serving diverse communities. The Illinois Credit Unions Act provides a framework for cooperative financial services. Illinois has been developing digital asset regulatory guidance through its state banking department.
laws.penalty: IDFPR can revoke licenses; unlicensed money transmission is a criminal offense
exceptions: Federal institutions regulated by OCC or Fed are exempt from state licensing

quiz.q: What major financial exchanges based in Chicago give Illinois outsized importance in global finance?
options: CME Group and CBOE (futures and options exchanges)
Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chicago divisions

laws.title: Illinois Food Handling Regulation Act & Chicago Food Code
laws.subtitle: Illinois and Chicago have layered food safety rules for one of America's largest food markets
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Food Handling Regulation Enforcement Act requires all food establishments to be permitted and inspected by local health departments. Illinois has specific regulations for the state's large meat processing industry. Illinois also passed a law in 2021 expanding cottage food options, allowing more categories of home-produced foods to be sold directly to consumers. The Illinois Department of Public Health collaborates with Chicago and other municipalities on inspections. Illinois participates in the FDA's Voluntary National Retail Food Regulatory Program Standards.

Food trucks have mobile food vehicle licenses distinct from fixed establishment

quiz.q: What role does Illinois play in the US food system beyond just its own food service regulations?
options: Is a major food production and distribution hub, including the Chicago Mercantile Exchange setting global commodity prices
Home of all major US food certification laboratories
Required state for all US organic certification
quiz.explanation: Illinois — particularly Chicago — is a critical hub of the US food system. The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) sets global prices for corn, soybeans, wheat, and cattle. Chicago has historically been a major meat processing center, and Illinois produces significant quantities of corn and soybeans.

laws.title: Illinois Humane Care for Animals Act
laws.subtitle: Comprehensive animal protection including tethering restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Humane Care for Animals Act (510 ILCS 70/) is one of the more comprehensive state animal welfare laws. It bans leaving animals in vehicles in dangerous temperatures, restricts tethering (dogs may not be tethered for more than 3 hours in 24 hours in adverse weather), and mandates food, water, and shelter for outdoor animals. Illinois also prohibits animal fighting, requires shelters to hold stray animals for a minimum period, and has a 'Pets in Danger' law allowing first responders to break into cars to rescue animals in life-threatening situations without liability. Cook County and Chicago add additional local protections.

exceptions: Farming and livestock operations under Illinois Livestock Management Facilities Act

Veterinary procedures

laws.title: Illinois Marriage and Dissolution of Marriage Act
laws.subtitle: Illinois uses income-shares child support and favors joint custody
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Marriage and Dissolution of Marriage Act (IMDMA) governs divorce and family law. Illinois is an equitable distribution state. Illinois uses the Income Shares Model for child support, calculating support based on both parents' combined income and dividing proportionally. Illinois has a strong presumption toward shared parental responsibilities ('allocation of parenting time') rather than sole custody. Illinois also has comprehensive domestic violence law — the Illinois Domestic Violence Act provides extensive protection orders. Same-sex marriage has been legal in Illinois since 2013.

Short-term marriages may get simplified procedures

Illinois made divorce require a jury trial
Illinois required DNA testing before allowing divorce
quiz.explanation: Illinois's 2016 IMDMA reform eliminated fault-based divorce grounds entirely, moving to a pure no-fault system where the only required finding is that the marriage is 'irretrievably broken.' This modernization eliminated the need to allege or prove misconduct like adultery or mental cruelty.

laws.title: Illinois Landlord-Tenant Rights & Property Tax Appeal
laws.subtitle: Residential tenant protections and assessment appeals
laws.fullDescription: Illinois does not have statewide rent control (preempted since 1997), but the Chicago Residential Landlord-Tenant Ordinance (RLTO) provides strong local protections including required security deposit interest, 30-day notice for lease termination, and tenant remedies for uninhabitable conditions. Illinois property owners can appeal assessments through the county Board of Review and the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board (PTAB). Cook County has a complex classification system affecting commercial property tax rates significantly.

exceptions: Chicago RLTO applies within city limits only
State law preempts rent control outside Chicago

quiz.q: What does Chicago's RLTO require landlords to pay on tenant security deposits?
quiz.explanation: Chicago's Residential Landlord-Tenant Ordinance requires landlords holding security deposits to pay interest on them at a rate set annually by the City Comptroller, a protection not found in most U.S. cities.

laws.title: Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act
laws.subtitle: Strong consumer fraud prohibitions with private right of action
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act (815 ILCS 505) prohibits unfair methods of competition, deceptive acts, and unfair practices in trade or commerce. Consumers can recover actual damages plus attorney fees; the AG can seek injunctions and civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation ($100,000 for elderly victims). Illinois also has robust debt collection protections under the Collection Agency Act and specific auto dealer rules. The Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA, 2008) — the nation's first and strongest biometric privacy law — has generated billions in class action settlements against companies using facial recognition and fingerprint data without consent.

exceptions: BIPA applies to fingerprints, retina scans, face geometry, voiceprints
AG penalties up to $100,000 for violations against elderly

quiz.q: What does Illinois's BIPA (Biometric Information Privacy Act) regulate that makes it uniquely powerful?
options: Biometric identifiers like fingerprints, face geometry, and retina scans
quiz.explanation: Illinois's BIPA (2008) regulates biometric identifiers — fingerprints, retina/iris scans, facial geometry, voiceprints, and hand scans. It requires written consent before collection and prohibits sale of biometrics, with per-violation damages that have led to billions in class-action settlements.

laws.title: Chicago Minimum Wage — $16.20/hour (2024)
laws.subtitle: Chicago Minimum Wage Ordinance — Higher than state
laws.fullDescription: Chicago has its own minimum wage higher than Illinois state law. In 2024, Chicago's minimum wage is $16.20/hour for large employers (21+ employees) and $15.80 for smaller employers. Illinois state minimum is $14/hour (2024), rising to $15 by 2025. Tipped workers have a separate minimum.
laws.penalty: Violations: back pay, $500/day fine, private civil action.
exceptions: Tipped workers minimum: $9.48/hour
Youth workers in training programs may have different rates
Small businesses have lower minimums with phased implementation

quiz.q: What is Chicago's minimum wage for large employers in 2024?
quiz.explanation: Chicago's 2024 minimum wage is $16.20/hour for large employers (21+ employees), above the Illinois state minimum of $14/hour.

laws.title: SAFE-T Act — Cashless Bail (2023)
laws.subtitle: Illinois Public Act 101-0652 — First state to end cash bail
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's SAFE-T Act, effective January 2023, eliminated cash bail — making Illinois the first state to do so. Defendants are either detained or released based on safety and flight risk assessments, not ability to pay bail. The law also strengthened use-of-force standards for police.
laws.penalty: Crimes still carry criminal penalties; only the pre-trial detention system changed.
exceptions: Detention still permitted for flight risks or dangers to the community
Serious charges like murder have stricter detention review
Crimes of violence trigger automatic detention hearings

quiz.q: What historic change did Illinois's SAFE-T Act make in 2023?
options: Required electronic monitoring for all releases
Transferred bail decisions to federal courts
quiz.explanation: Illinois became the first US state to completely eliminate cash bail in 2023. Pre-trial detention decisions are now based on risk assessment, not ability to pay.

laws.title: Cannabis Legalization — Adult Use (2020)
laws.subtitle: Illinois Cannabis Regulation and Tax Act
laws.fullDescription: Illinois legalized recreational cannabis in January 2020. Adults 21+ can purchase up to 30g flower, 5g concentrate, or 500mg THC edibles per transaction. Illinois had the first state-run social equity cannabis program, expunging prior convictions. Tax rates are among the highest in the US (25–41%).
laws.penalty: Possession over legal limits: civil fine $200–$2,500. Underage use: criminal charge.
exceptions: Purchase limits differ for residents vs. non-residents
Home cultivation allowed for medical patients only
Driving under cannabis influence is still DUI

quiz.q: What made Illinois's cannabis legalization unique?
options: First state-run social equity program with automatic expungements
quiz.explanation: Illinois was first to legalize recreational cannabis through the legislature (not ballot initiative) and included the nation's first social equity provisions with automatic expungement of prior cannabis convictions.

laws.title: Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA)
laws.subtitle: Illinois BIPA 740 ILCS 14 — Strictest biometric law in US
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's BIPA (2008) is the nation's strictest biometric privacy law, regulating collection, use, and storage of fingerprints, retinal scans, facial geometry, and voiceprints by private companies. Companies must obtain written consent. Statutory damages of $1,000–$5,000 per violation have resulted in massive class actions.
laws.penalty: $1,000 per negligent violation, $5,000 per intentional violation. Class actions worth hundreds of millions.
exceptions: Government entities not covered — applies to private companies
Photography does not constitute biometric data collection
Medical providers collecting for healthcare treatment

quiz.q: What is the statutory damages amount for an intentional BIPA violation?
quiz.explanation: Illinois BIPA provides $5,000 per intentional or reckless violation and $1,000 per negligent violation. These damages have led to class action settlements worth hundreds of millions.

laws.title: Chicago RLTO — Tenant-Friendly Landlord Laws
laws.subtitle: Chicago Residential Landlord and Tenant Ordinance
laws.fullDescription: Chicago's RLTO (1986) is one of the nation's most tenant-friendly landlord-tenant laws. Landlords must provide written leases, maintain habitable conditions, return security deposits with interest (if held over 6 months), and give proper notice. Tenants may withhold rent or make repairs-and-deduct for violations.
laws.penalty: Security deposit violations: landlord pays 2x deposit plus attorney's fees.
exceptions: Owner-occupied buildings with 6 or fewer units exempt
CHA (public housing) has separate regulations
Condos sold as owner-occupied not covered

quiz.q: What must Chicago landlords do with security deposits held for over 6 months?
quiz.explanation: Chicago's RLTO requires landlords holding security deposits for 6+ months to pay interest on them. Violations can result in the landlord owing 2x the deposit to tenants.

laws.title: Chicago Speed Camera Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Chicago Code Chapter 9-102 — Automated school/park zones
laws.fullDescription: Chicago operates hundreds of automated speed cameras in school and park safety zones. Cameras issue $35 fines for 6-10 mph over the limit and $100 for 11+ mph over. The system generates hundreds of millions in revenue annually. No points added to driver's license.
laws.penalty: First offense in school zone 6–10 mph over: $35. 11+ mph: $100.
exceptions: Fines not added to driving record — civil penalty only
Payment plans available for low-income drivers
Cameras require proper certification and calibration
laws.sourceLabel: City of Chicago Speed Camera Program

quiz.q: At what speed over the limit does Chicago's school zone speed camera issue its first fine?
quiz.explanation: Chicago's school zone speed cameras issue a $35 fine for driving 6–10 mph over the speed limit and $100 for 11+ mph over.

laws.title: Illinois Climate & Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) 2021
laws.subtitle: Public Act 102-0662 — 100% clean energy by 2045
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's CEJA (2021) sets a goal of 100% clean energy by 2045. It created new renewable energy credits, environmental justice provisions for communities near power plants, $580M in labor transition funding, and requires coal plants to retire by 2035. Illinois's nuclear power fleet is supported with ZEC credits.
laws.penalty: Utilities not meeting clean energy standards face penalties and compliance costs.
exceptions: Nuclear plants receive zero-emission credit support
Natural gas plants get longer phase-out timelines
Industrial processes have separate allowances

quiz.q: What year does Illinois's CEJA target for 100% clean energy?
quiz.explanation: Illinois's Climate & Equitable Jobs Act sets 2045 as the target for 100% clean energy, with coal plants retiring by 2035.

laws.title: Abortion Rights Enshrined in Illinois Law
laws.subtitle: Illinois Reproductive Health Act (2019)
laws.fullDescription: Illinois codified abortion rights into state law in 2019 with the Reproductive Health Act, repealing a 1975 Abortion Act. Illinois explicitly recognizes a 'fundamental right' to abortion. After Dobbs (2022), Illinois became a destination state for abortion access, with 'shield laws' protecting providers.
laws.penalty: N/A — This law protects access. Violations of provider rights: civil liability.
exceptions: Illinois has no gestational limits in state law
Conscience rights for providers who object
Parental notice act applies in certain cases

quiz.q: What did Illinois's 2019 Reproductive Health Act do?
options: Codified abortion as a fundamental right
quiz.explanation: Illinois's 2019 Reproductive Health Act explicitly recognized abortion as a fundamental right, making Illinois one of the strongest abortion-access states.

laws.title: Prevailing Wage Act — Union-Rate Requirements
laws.subtitle: Illinois Prevailing Wage Act 820 ILCS 130
laws.fullDescription: Illinois requires workers on public construction projects to be paid the locally prevailing (union) wage for each trade. Wage determinations are set by the Department of Labor. Applies to state, county, and municipal projects. Illinois has strong union labor traditions, especially in Chicago.
laws.penalty: Willful violations: class A misdemeanor, debarment from public projects.
exceptions: Projects under $2,500 threshold may be exempt
Emergency repairs have modified procedures
Federal Davis-Bacon Act applies to federally funded projects
laws.sourceLabel: Illinois Department of Labor — Prevailing Wage

quiz.q: What determines the 'prevailing wage' rate for Illinois public construction?
options: The locally prevailing (typically union) wage for each trade
quiz.explanation: Illinois's Prevailing Wage Act requires payment of locally prevailing wages — typically set at union scale for each specific trade — on all public construction projects.

laws.title: Automatic Voter Registration — Illinois (2017)
laws.subtitle: Illinois Election Code — AVR at state agencies
laws.fullDescription: Illinois implemented automatic voter registration in 2017 — eligible citizens are automatically registered when they interact with state agencies like the DMV. Early voting begins 40 days before elections. Vote by mail is available to any registered voter. Illinois has no-excuse absentee voting.
laws.penalty: Voter fraud: Class 3 felony.
exceptions: Illinois residents overseas use UOCAVA rules
Voters in county jail may vote if not convicted
Felons who have served their sentence can register

quiz.q: When did Illinois implement automatic voter registration?
quiz.explanation: Illinois implemented automatic voter registration (AVR) in 2017, registering eligible citizens automatically when they interact with Secretary of State's office (DMV) and other agencies.

laws.title: Cook County Property Tax — Triennial Reassessment
laws.subtitle: Cook County Assessor — Rotating township reassessment
laws.fullDescription: Cook County (Chicago) has a unique property tax system where properties are reassessed every three years on a rotating township schedule. Illinois has a Property Tax Extension Limitation Law (PTELL) capping levy increases at 5% or CPI. Cook County property taxes are among the nation's highest.
laws.penalty: Non-payment: penalties, interest, and eventual tax deed sale.
exceptions: Senior citizens' assessment freeze
Veterans exemptions
Homeowner exemption reduces assessed value by $10,000

quiz.q: How often are Cook County properties typically reassessed?
quiz.explanation: Cook County properties are reassessed on a triennial (three-year) rotating schedule by township.

laws.title: Illinois Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
laws.subtitle: Illinois FOIA 5 ILCS 140 — Public records access
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's FOIA gives public access to government records. Agencies must respond within 5 business days (extendable to 10). Denied requesters may appeal to the Public Access Counselor (PAC) at the AG's office. Illinois has a public interest exception.
laws.penalty: Willful refusal: civil lawsuit; agency may pay attorney's fees and fines up to $5,000.
exceptions: Privacy exemptions for personal information
Law enforcement investigation records
Trade secrets and proprietary business information

quiz.q: What government office handles Illinois FOIA appeal disputes?
options: Public Access Counselor at the AG's office
quiz.explanation: Illinois FOIA appeals go to the Public Access Counselor (PAC) at the Illinois Attorney General's office, which can review denials and issue binding opinions.

laws.title: AllKids — Health Insurance Regardless of Immigration Status
laws.subtitle: Illinois AllKids program — Coverage for all children
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's AllKids program provides health insurance to all children regardless of immigration status. Premiums and copays are on a sliding scale based on income. Illinois was among the first states to provide health coverage for undocumented children. Illinois also expanded Medicaid to adults up to 138% FPL.
laws.penalty: N/A — This is a benefit program.
exceptions: Premium requirements vary by income level
Adults without documentation have more limited access
Federal Medicaid funds cannot cover non-citizens — state funds used
laws.sourceLabel: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services

quiz.q: What makes Illinois's AllKids health insurance program distinctive?
options: It provides coverage to all children regardless of immigration status
It requires no premiums for anyone
quiz.explanation: Illinois's AllKids program provides health insurance to ALL children regardless of immigration status, with premiums on a sliding scale.

laws.title: Chicago RTA — Regional Transit Authority
laws.subtitle: Regional Transportation Authority Act
laws.fullDescription: Chicago's transit has a three-tier structure: RTA (Regional Transportation Authority) oversees funding; CTA (Chicago Transit Authority) runs city buses and trains; Metra operates commuter rail; Pace handles suburban buses. Illinois law gives these agencies taxing authority and bonding authority.
laws.penalty: Fare evasion: $100–$300 citation. Assault on transit employees: class 4 felony.
exceptions: Low-income riders qualify for reduced fares
Seniors 65+ pay half fare on CTA
Disabled riders with ADA accommodations have reduced fares

quiz.q: Which organization oversees funding for Chicago's regional transit system?
quiz.explanation: The RTA (Regional Transportation Authority) oversees funding and coordination for Chicago's regional transit system, which includes CTA, Metra, and Pace.

laws.title: Lead Service Line Replacement Act
laws.subtitle: Illinois Public Act 102-0613 — Mandatory replacement by 2037
laws.fullDescription: Illinois enacted one of the nation's most comprehensive lead service line replacement programs in 2021. Water utilities must inventory and replace lead service lines by 2037. Illinois has one of the highest concentrations of lead service lines in the US. Chicago has the most lead service lines of any US city.
laws.penalty: Utilities not meeting replacement timelines: IEPA enforcement and fines.
exceptions: Schools with lead pipes get priority replacement
Income-based assistance for private-side replacement
Some older pipes may be relined rather than replaced

quiz.q: By what year must Illinois water utilities replace all lead service lines?
quiz.explanation: Illinois's Lead Service Line Replacement Act requires water utilities to replace all lead service lines by 2037. Chicago has more lead service lines than any US city.

laws.title: Illinois Human Rights Act — Broad Protections
laws.subtitle: Illinois Human Rights Act 775 ILCS 5
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination in employment, housing, and public accommodations. Protected classes include race, sex, age (40+), disability, national origin, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, and source of income. Illinois has broader protections than federal law in many areas.
laws.penalty: Illinois Human Rights Commission can award back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney's fees.
exceptions: Religious organizations have some hiring exemptions
BFOQ (bona fide occupational qualification) defense
Small employers have limited exemptions in some cases

quiz.q: Under Illinois's Human Rights Act, what is the minimum age protected from employment discrimination?
quiz.explanation: Illinois's Human Rights Act protects workers 40 and older from age discrimination, following the federal ADEA standard. Illinois's act also covers more protected classes than federal law.

laws.title: Illinois Workers' Compensation — Exclusive Remedy
laws.subtitle: Illinois Workers' Compensation Act
laws.fullDescription: Illinois employers must carry workers' compensation insurance. Injured employees receive benefits (medical, wage replacement) regardless of fault but cannot sue the employer in civil court (exclusive remedy). Illinois has relatively generous workers' comp benefits with high wage replacement rates.
laws.penalty: Employers without insurance: business license suspension, fines up to $500/day.
exceptions: Intentional employer harm can still result in civil lawsuit
Employers with fewer than one employee may be exempt in some sectors
Federal employees have separate workers' comp system

quiz.q: What does the 'exclusive remedy' rule mean in Illinois workers' compensation?
options: Workers can only be injured once
Workers get benefits but generally cannot sue the employer in civil court
Employers must provide exclusive medical care
Only state hospitals can treat work injuries
quiz.explanation: The exclusive remedy rule means workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy for workplace injuries — injured employees receive guaranteed benefits but typically cannot sue their employer.

laws.title: Illinois Anti-SLAPP Law — Citizen Participation Act
laws.subtitle: Illinois Citizen Participation Act 735 ILCS 110
laws.fullDescription: Illinois's Citizen Participation Act (2007) protects people from SLAPP suits — Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation. If a lawsuit is brought primarily to silence participation in government or public affairs, defendants can file a motion to dismiss and courts may award attorney's fees.
laws.penalty: Filing a SLAPP suit: dismissal, attorney's fees, costs awarded to defendant.
exceptions: Genuine business disputes aren't covered
Government entities suing for regulatory enforcement
Claims not related to protected petitioning activity

quiz.q: What does 'SLAPP' stand for in Illinois law?
quiz.explanation: SLAPP stands for Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation — lawsuits designed to silence critics through litigation costs. Illinois's Citizen Participation Act allows quick dismissal.

laws.title: Pharmacist Prescribing Authority — Illinois
laws.subtitle: Illinois Pharmacy Practice Act — Collaborative prescribing
laws.fullDescription: Illinois allows pharmacists to prescribe some medications including hormonal contraceptives and certain vaccines under collaborative practice agreements with physicians. Illinois was among the first states to allow pharmacist-prescribed oral contraceptives, expanding access to care.
laws.penalty: Practicing without license: class 4 felony. Dispensing errors: civil malpractice, licensing sanctions.
exceptions: Pharmacist interns can fill under supervision
Emergency prescription dispensing for 30 days without new Rx allowed
Certain OTC medications don't require prescription

quiz.q: What unique prescribing authority do Illinois pharmacists have?
options: They can prescribe hormonal contraceptives and certain vaccines under collaborative practice
quiz.explanation: Illinois pharmacists can prescribe hormonal contraceptives and administer certain vaccines under collaborative practice agreements with physicians.

laws.title: Plastic Bag Fee & Statewide Restriction
laws.subtitle: Chicago/Illinois regulations — Sustainable packaging
laws.fullDescription: Chicago banned single-use plastic bags at large retailers in 2015. Illinois passed a statewide plastic bag fee starting 2024. Chicago also restricts polystyrene foam food containers. Retailers must charge 7 cents per single-use bag. The state law phases out non-compostable bags by 2026.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant retailers: fines starting at $100/day.
exceptions: Produce bags, dry cleaning bags remain exempt
Small retailers have extended compliance timelines
Reusable bags encouraged as substitute

quiz.q: When did Chicago first ban single-use plastic bags at large retailers?
quiz.explanation: Chicago banned single-use plastic bags at large retailers in 2015. Illinois later passed a statewide law phasing in restrictions from 2024.
